newsitem.title: USA: Late-season tropical storm in Caribbean kills two.
newsitem.headline: Late-season tropical storm in Caribbean kills two.

text.p: Tropical Storm Marco trekked slowly through the Caribbean Tuesday after leaving two people dead in Nicaragua.
Forecasters said could it could reach Jamaica, Cuba and the island of Hispaniola, shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, later this week.

At 7 p.m. EST (2400 GMT), Marco was near latitude 13.7 north and longitude 79.9 west, about 360 miles (576 km) southwest of Kingston, Jamaica, and moving southeastward at five mph (12 kph), the National Hurricane Center said.

Nicaraguan civil defense authorities blamed at least two deaths on Marco after flooding that washed away homes in the Pacific coast and northern regions. They said one person had died in a traffic accident and another by drowning.
Maximum sustained winds were 60 mph (95 kph). Tropical storm force winds extended up to 105 miles (165 km) from Marco's center.
Forecasters warned that more heavy rains in Central America could unleash flash floods and mudslides.

A tropical storm watch was in effect for Jamaica and forecasters said all of the western and central Caribbean region, particularly Jamaica, Cuba and the island of Hispaniola should monitor the storm's progress.
"All the models are taking this tropical storm toward Jamaica and then toward eastern Cuba," Avila said.

Tropical storm watches indicate forecasters believe tropical storm conditions could threaten coastal areas within 36 hours. Tropical depressions become tropical storms when sustained winds top 39 mph (62 kph). A tropical storm graduates to hurricane status when its maximum winds exceed 74 mph (119 kph).
This year's Atlantic hurricane season officially ends on Nov. 30.
